summary: Deploy-time optimizer snapshot playback failing; need guided fallback and safe traffic playback
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when applying an optimizer snapshot during a rolling deploy (microbatch + prefix-kv + mixed-quant profile) live traffic playback fails with persistent 5xxs and streaming disconnects. Impact: Production traffic for two critical endpoints is seeing ~20% request errors and token-level latency spikes (95p increase). Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-west, nodes running 4x A10G pools, optimizer snapshot created from a canary run. Ask: Provide guided steps to safely playback the snapshot for rollback testing and an emergency fallback procedure that minimizes churn and latency regression.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Push optimizer snapshot ID snap-2026-03-11-17 applied via console canary plan
2) Route 10% live traffic to canary pool with microbatch enabled and kv-prefetch enabled
3) Observe canary health: streaming disconnects after initial token streaming and 5xx surge on route /v1/generate
4) Increase traffic to 30% to attempt full rollout - errors broaden to primary pool and autoscaler triggers rebalancing
logs: 2026-03-12T17:20:03Z ERROR serving-runtime: response writer dropped, connection reset by peer, request_id=ccf3-9a2
2026-03-12T17:20:08Z WARN scheduler: batch flush failed: kv-evict triggered during active sequence, pool=dedicated-uswest-4
2026-03-12T17:20:12Z ERROR optimize: quant-profile-apply failed on node node-13: kernel mismatch, attempting fallback
2026-03-12T17:20:22Z ERROR api-gateway: 502 upstream read timeout on /v1/generate, trace=trx-55b
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: optimizer snapshot combined microbatch + aggressive kv-prefetch + mixed quant profile causing kernel codepaths mismatch on a subset of nodes (heterogeneous GPU drivers across pool).
Telemetry: 95p token latency rose from 420ms -> 920ms after snapshot, error rate spike correlates with nodes that had driver version 510.56.8; nodes with driver 515.x remained stable.

Observed autoscaler churn: rebalancer attempted to spin up replacement nodes while eviction was active leading to transient state where some requests hit partially-initialized runtime and failed with 5xx.
Console trace: rollout plan attempted snapshot playback without explicit kernel-compatibility check; snapshot metadata lacks node-driver-min field.
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Reached out to customer for exact snapshot ID and traffic split. Asked to hold further rollout and reduce canary to 0% until we confirm safe playback plan.
Customer (Kaleida): Confirmed snapshot snap-2026-03-11-17 and asked for step-by-step rollback that doesn't require full cluster drain — high availability requirement.

Ravi Kapoor (SRE): Noted mismatch in GPU driver versions; recommending snapshot replay in a controlled shadow environment and forced kernel fallback for nodes with older drivers. Opening issue for runtime kernel selector change.

Ravi Kapoor (SRE): Proposed immediate mitigation — set route-level fallback to redwood-tuned-7b-fp16 and pause optimizer feature flags for that tenant, then gradually reintroduce microbatch with conservative batch_size cap=4.
resolution: Workaround applied: support paused the canary (reverted traffic to 0%), enabled per-route model fallback to redwood-tuned-7b-fp16 for affected endpoints, and temporarily disabled kv-prefetch and microbatch for Kaleida's tenant via per-tenant flags. Customer traffic stabilized and error rate dropped to baseline within 6 minutes. Next steps: SRE will add kernel-compatibility checks to snapshot metadata, add a conservative preflight that runs snapshot in a shadow pool with 2-minute warmup, and create an automated safe-playback checklist in Console. Follow-up task created to roll kernel-selector patch and schedule a controlled re-run with driver-aligned nodes. Customer agreed to a coordinated maintenance window for re-introduction.
